title: The Verb εἰμί
subtitle: The most common verb in Greek — to be.
objectives: Conjugate εἰμί in the present indicative: all persons, both numbers.
Understand that εἰμί is used for existence, predication, and identity.
Recognize the forms εἰμί, εἶ, ἐστί, ἐσμέν, ἐστέ, εἰσί on sight.
Translate sentences with εἰμί into natural English.

sections.heading: The verb εἰμί
sections.body:
εἰμί (I am) is the most common verb in Greek prose. It is irregular. The present indicative forms do not follow the regular pattern of thematic verbs (which you will learn in the next lesson). You must memorize them.

εἰμί is used to express existence ('there is'), predication ('Socrates is wise'), and identity ('Socrates is the teacher'). It links a subject to a predicate noun or adjective. ὁ Σωκράτης σοφός ἐστιν — 'Socrates is wise.' σοφός is a predicate adjective in the nominative, agreeing with the subject.

sections.heading: The present indicative of εἰμί
sections.body:
singular
  1st   εἰμί        I am
  2nd   εἶ          you are
  3rd   ἐστί(ν)     he/she/it is

  plural
  1st   ἐσμέν       we are
  2nd   ἐστέ        you (plural) are
  3rd   εἰσί(ν)     they are

The third person forms ἐστί and εἰσί add a movable ν when the next word begins with a vowel or when the verb ends a sentence. ἐστὶν ἀνήρ — 'there is a man.' εἰσὶν ἄνθρωποι — 'there are men.'

The verb is often enclitic (it leans on the preceding word and loses its accent). In practice, you will often see ἐστιν written without an accent when it is not the first word in its clause.

sections.heading: Examples from Plato
sections.body:
Plato, Apology 20c: σοφὸς γάρ εἰμι.
'For I am wise.' γάρ is a postpositive particle ('for'); the word order is flexible.

Plato, Crito 43b: Σωκράτης ἐστὶν ὁ σοφώτατος.
'Socrates is the wisest.' ὁ σοφώτατος is a superlative adjective in the nominative, agreeing with the subject Σωκράτης.

sections.heading: Self-check
sections.instructions: Cover the answers. Give the requested form or answer the question.

items.prompt: When do you add the movable ν?
items.answer: When the next word begins with a vowel or when the verb ends a sentence.

sections.heading: Up next
sections.body: Lesson 2.11 introduces the present indicative active of regular ω-verbs: λύω, λύεις, λύει, λύομεν, λύετε, λύουσι. These are the thematic verbs, and they follow a predictable pattern. Once you have this conjugation, you have the foundation for all Greek verb forms.

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark the lesson complete when you can conjugate εἰμί from memory in under thirty seconds and can translate ten sentences with εἰμί without error.
